object_description: compact two-story volume with integrated courtyard and shed-like rooflights
design_condition: The compact volume is positioned with sufficient distance from adjacent buildings, accessed from a new western road, and filtered from neighbouring residences by tree planting while incorporating the vehicle lock and walking yard.

positive.statement: The compact new building fits into the overall complex and remains spatially compatible with the adjacent buildings.
Tree plantings provide a spatial filter to the neighbouring residential buildings.
The western development route and existing parking make the address accessible to visitors and deliveries.
The wooden facades create a homely overall impression and a facade compatible with the environment.
The compact volume makes the project cost-effective.
A friendly atmosphere is created through the urban development and the architecture of the facades and roof.
The walking yard gains a sense of scale through its connecting staircase to the living floor.

negative.statement: The walking yard could be problematically visible from the neighbouring residential buildings.
The shed-like rooflight design does not correspond to the building structure, floor plan or section.
Separating the patient rooms and lounges from the walking yard by a covered external staircase is negative in terms of safety.
Winding corridors and distant rooms require considerable monitoring work during operation.
The north orientation of the intensive-care rooms is problematic.
The floor plan has major deficiencies in use and safety.
